candidateDecisions.label: Educational minor in computer-science teaching
candidateDecisions.assessment: The official educational minor includes subject didactics and supervised secondary-school teaching. Rhetoric and software study do not supply that teaching progression.

analysis: Programming and discrete logic establish formal and practical foundations. Databases, networks and operating systems support relational and connected systems, including concurrency, memory and scheduling. Software Development builds C++ and Haskell programmes and uses code review, testing and design patterns. Data structures precede advanced algorithms, while linear algebra supports algorithms, statistics and data work. Numerical methods add computational modelling, and machine learning precedes neural networks and reinforcement learning. Image processing develops an OpenCV recognition pipeline and differs from graphics synthesis. Optimisation, probabilistic decisions and evaluated learning agents provide further advanced computing work. Research methods overlap through inference, experiments and technical reporting. Product design, philosophy, rhetoric and ethics complement software decisions and audience communication. The three informal Utrecht elective bundles reinforce the same option. The formal game route was compared with UCR vision, programming, learning agents and prototyping; it requires a continuing emphasis on game design and related game development that this catalogue does not sustain as a distinct option. The teaching minor needs subject didactics and supervised school work. The 24 retained selections materially address the target core. The software construction and networking courses offer real Haskell and concurrency content, while Utrecht has dedicated courses and a required client team project. Three unavailable placements were resolved with compensating moves, retaining all courses.

alignment.rationale: Both develop imperative programming and problem solving. UCR uses Python.
Both develop formal logic for computer science. UCR also covers discrete mathematics and proof.
Both study data structures and algorithms for organising and searching data.
Both develop advanced algorithm design and analysis.
Both develop statistical tools for research. Utrecht also teaches computer-science research design, literature review and reporting.
UCR’s Software Development course introduces functional programming in Haskell. Utrecht gives the subject a separate required course.
UCR’s Networks & Operating Systems course introduces processes, threads and concurrency. Utrecht gives concurrency a separate advanced course.
Both cover computer networks. UCR also examines operating systems, while Utrecht gives dedicated attention to computer architecture.
Both study relational databases. UCR includes SQL, normalisation and query processing.
Both develop software construction and testing. UCR combines C++ and Haskell with version control and code review.
Utrecht applies introductory computing in a dedicated project. UCR’s product design course contributes related prototyping practice.
Utrecht offers IT law as a major elective. UCR’s AI Ethics addresses privacy, fairness and accountability from an ethical perspective.
Utrecht offers a dedicated Web Technology elective.
Utrecht requires a 15 EC team software project for a client. UCR’s optional independent research is separate from the scheduled courses.
Choose 45 EC, including at least 15 EC at intermediate or advanced level. An optional individual thesis can count here.
Both develop data analysis. Utrecht also covers information retrieval.
UCR studies image processing and recognition. Utrecht’s graphics course focuses on generating images with computer graphics.
Both develop methods for intelligent systems. UCR focuses on decisions and reasoning under uncertainty.
